# Candidate module designs
- Module-D2: large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter.
- Module-D3: wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout.
- Module-D1: compact SiPM tile array.

# Thermal-cycling tests
Batches of 40 modules of each design were cycled 20 times between 300 K and 87 K.
Fraction failed (open channels or delamination):
- Module-D2: 30%  (the thin light-guide bonding cracks on cooldown)
- Module-D3: 2%
- Module-D1: 0.5%
Requirement: at most 5% failures after 20 cycles.

# Meeting notes 2026-01-20
Cabling feedthroughs were reviewed; enough feedthroughs are available for up to 30% coverage.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 20% coverage)
Light collection: Module-D2 38 PE/MeV, Module-D3 27 PE/MeV, Module-D1 18 PE/MeV. It rises with coverage, roughly as coverage^0.8.

content.text: D2 fails robustness. Choose between D3 and D1; D3 likely higher. Simulate at 30%.

input.justification: D2 has the highest light yield but fails thermal cycling (30% failed against a 5% limit). Modules can't be accessed after the cryostat is filled, so D2 is excluded. D3 has the next-highest yield and passes thermal cycling at 2% failed. 30% coverage is the maximum allowed and the feedthroughs support it. D3 at 30% simulates to 36.5 PE/MeV. I did not simulate D1 at 30%. The 2025 summary gave D1 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage against 27 for D3, so I expect D1 to be lower.

requirements.evidence: D3 at 30% simulates to 36.5 PE/MeV. This is the best among designs that pass robustness. D2 is higher but is excluded. D1 was not simulated at 30%, and the 2025 data at 20% put it below D3.
